chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Laythi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sharooti narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Oaf informed me, from Maymun, saying: Al-Bara ibn Azib informed me

He said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the digging of the ditch, a great, hard boulder appeared across the ditch which the pickaxes could not break. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came, and when he saw it, he took off his shirt, picked up the pickaxe, and said: 'In the Name of Allah.' He struck it once and broke one third of it. He said: 'Allah is Great. I have been given the keys to Syria. By Allah, I can now see its red palaces.' Then he struck a second time and said: 'In the Name of Allah,' and it split another third. He said: 'Allah is Great. I have been given the keys to Persia. By Allah, I can see the White Palace of Al-Mada'in.' Then he struck a third time and broke the remainder of the stone. He said: 'Allah is Great. I have been given the keys to Yemen. By Allah, I can see the gates of Sana'a from this place of mine.'

key_terms.الشَّام: Syria, a region in the Levant.
key_terms.الْخَنْدَق: The Ditch (Khandaq), a defensive trench dug by Muslims during the Battle of the Ditch.
key_terms.الْمَدَائِن: Al-Mada'in (Ctesiphon), the ancient capital of Persia.
key_terms.صَنْعَاء: Sana'a, the capital city of Yemen.
key_terms.مَفَاتِيح: Keys, metaphorically meaning authority, conquest, or access.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) say about the keys to Syria, Persia, and Yemen when striking the rock during the Battle of the Ditch?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Khisal, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) strikes a massive boulder during the Battle of the Ditch, revealing the future conquests of Syria, Persia, and Yemen as divine promises. Shia scholarship often interprets these 'keys' not merely as military victories but as the opening of spiritual and political authority, linking the physical breaking of the stone to the removal of barriers for the spread of Islam. This event underscores the concept of divine foreknowledge and the tangible manifestation of prophetic power in historical events.
